title: The Transcendental Reals are an Explicit Dense Gδ
description: Strengthens the parent's 'transcendentals are residual' to the explicit structural statement that the transcendental reals {x : ℝ | ¬ IsAlgebraic ℚ x} are themselves a concrete dense Gδ set — the named residual witness requested by the parent's open question. Proves the abstract lemma that in any T1 space the complement of a countable set is a Gδ (a countable intersection of open singleton-complements), and that in a perfect T1 Baire space it is moreover dense. As a dual corollary it establishes the analogue of 'ℚ is not a Gδ': the algebraic reals, being dense yet meagre, are not a Gδ set.

overview: The parent entry 'The Algebraic Reals are Meagre' shows the transcendentals are residual (comeagre) and therefore dense. But 'residual' is, by definition, only membership in the filter generated by dense Gδ sets — it names no concrete witness. This entry closes that gap by exhibiting the transcendentals as themselves a concrete dense Gδ: writing the algebraic reals as a countable set A, the transcendentals are exactly ⋂_{a ∈ A} {a}ᶜ, a countable intersection of open sets (each {a}ᶜ is open since ℝ is T1), dense because its complement A is meagre. The construction is abstracted to its natural generality (T1 ⟹ countable complement is Gδ; perfect T1 Baire ⟹ dense Gδ), mirroring Mathlib's treatment of the irrationals. A dual corollary establishes the analogue of 'ℚ is not a Gδ': the algebraic reals, being a dense meagre set, cannot be a Gδ, since a dense Gδ is residual and no nonempty Baire space carries a set that is simultaneously meagre and residual.

conclusion.summary: A 165-line, 0-sorry, 0-axiom formalization exhibiting the transcendental reals as an explicit dense Gδ set in ℝ — the concrete residual witness requested by the parent's open question — built on a reusable abstract lemma that the complement of a countable set is a Gδ in any T1 space (and a dense Gδ in a perfect T1 Baire space). A dual corollary proves the algebraic reals are not a Gδ, the analogue of the classical fact that ℚ is not a Gδ.
conclusion.implications: Being a dense Gδ is a strict topological strengthening of being residual: residual asserts only that a set contains a dense Gδ, whereas here the transcendentals are exhibited as one. The pairing transcendentals = dense Gδ versus algebraic reals = dense Fσ that is not Gδ is the exact analogue of irrationals/rationals, placing the algebraic-transcendental dichotomy alongside Mathlib's irrational/rational one. The abstract lemmas isGδ_compl_of_countable and not_isGδ_of_dense_isMeagre are reusable for any countable / dense-meagre set in suitable spaces.
openQuestions: Dualize to the algebraic reals as an explicit Fσ (countable union of closed singletons) and record the full Gδ/Fσ classification of the dichotomy.
Quantify the dense Gδ further: exhibit an explicit decreasing sequence of dense open sets whose intersection is the transcendentals, making the Gδ presentation fully constructive.
